WHY: The plan keeps a software encoder as a rescue/unsupported-hardware option — opt-in, visibly CPU-limited, negotiating lower geometry/frame-rate instead of silently consuming all cores — and names oxideav-h265 as a legitimate pure-Rust candidate to EVALUATE (its README claims an I/P/B encoder at 8-bit 4:2:0 with dimensions divisible by 16; claims are things to verify, not evidence). This bead preserves that feature without letting it touch the critical path.

SCOPE: (1) Define the opt-in software profile behind the fr-media contracts: explicit selection only (hardware-required deployments fail typed instead), enforced geometry/frame-rate ceilings, visible CPU-cost reporting in diagnostics. (2) Evaluate candidates at a pinned revision each: x265 (GPL/commercial licensing and patent considerations recorded — placing it in a plugin/process does NOT automatically settle redistribution; the shipped combination needs a recorded distribution decision) and oxideav-h265 (independent decoder interoperability, supported bitstream subset, adversarial-input behavior, throughput/memory/quality at matched bitrate, browser-target build sanity). (3) Write the adopt/defer/reject decision note with measurements.

CONSTRAINTS: no second runtime or large multimedia stack smuggled in; no uncapped optimization project; the replaceable media interface is the boundary; DECISION from the plan stands — no HEVC encoder written from scratch.

ACCEPTANCE: the evaluation report with retained runs and the licensing/distribution analysis; if adopted, the profile ships with its own capability row and CPU-envelope disclosure; if not, the negative evidence is recorded and the profile stays absent. Provenance: plan sections 8.1, 9.3, 9.4, 25.
close_reason: Software HEVC encoder evaluation complete. Documented in docs/decisions/0004-software-encoder-profile.md (ADR 0004) and docs/software-encoder-evaluation.md. Evaluated oxideav-h265 v0.0.10 (valid Main 8-bit bitstream verified by FFprobe 8.0.1; measured release throughput 0.41 fps at 320x240, orders of magnitude too slow for real-time streaming; retained as offline test tool only) and x265 (rejected due to GPL distribution risks and HEVC patent royalties). Defined constraints for opt-in developer profile (Backend::SoftwareExplicit: <=1280x720, <=30 fps, visible CPU reporting; zero silent fallback).

title: Version 1 release: signed artifacts reproducing tested behavior
description:
WHY: The definition of done: install a small process family on a supported host already on Tailscale, grant OS permissions, and use the desktop from qualified native desktop, mobile, and browser clients — no account, no pairing — with every failure honest and every claim evidenced.

EXIT CRITERIA: signed/notarized macOS family, signed Windows packages, reproducible Linux package, mobile store-signed builds, browser assets versioned with the protocol — all built by repository-owned commands through the dsr lanes; installation artifacts reproduce the tested behavior (release-candidate re-run of the fault and security suites on the shipped binaries); unsupported states fail specifically; no performance claim outruns retained evidence; license/provenance manifests complete for every native component (FFmpeg configuration and license notices, opus, the Windows audio component, platform SDKs) with the distribution decision recorded; the v1.4 completion rules honored — expired input never executes, approval gates observation, shared encoders outlive subscribers, recovery works under the advertised loss envelope, browser idle/flush and endpoint-audio scopes have qualification evidence; codebase under the 240k ceiling by the fixed counting command.

Provenance: plan sections 20.3, 23 Phase 5, 26.

title: Workspace bootstrap: root Cargo.toml plus fr-core first slice (typed IDs, generations, limits)
description:
WHY: Everything else in the project consumes typed identifiers and one tested limits structure, and the cargo workspace cannot exist safely without its first real crate (a virtual workspace with zero members breaks every cargo command in the checkout — verified empirically before this tracker existed).

SCOPE: In ONE commit, create the root Cargo.toml (resolver "3", members = ["crates/*"], [workspace.package] edition 2024 + license-file, [workspace.dependencies] with asupersync pinned default-features=false and an fr-core path entry, workspace lints with unsafe_code = "forbid"), Cargo.lock, and crates/fr-core with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] as line 1. fr-core's first vertical slice: (a) distinct newtype identifiers for host boot, OS session, remote session, input lease, display geometry, codec configuration, recovery generation, and viewport mapping — deliberately NOT interchangeable, no raw u64s crossing module boundaries; (b) the single limits structure holding the protocol/resource ceilings: 64 KiB ordinary control message, 1 MiB clipboard item, 16 MiB max encoded access unit, 8192 max per axis, 16,777,216 max coded pixels, 2-12 picture reassembly window, 32 MiB per-viewer compressed budget — all as negotiate-downward ceilings with checked arithmetic helpers that validate length/stride/product before any allocation.

CONSTRAINTS: Asupersync is the only runtime dependency. No unsafe. Never leave a directory under crates/ without a manifest, even briefly.

ACCEPTANCE: cargo fmt/check/clippy/test green; unit tests prove identifier non-interchangeability (compile-fail tests where practical), ceiling validation rejects over-limit and overflow-adjacent values, and the limits structure round-trips its negotiated-downward logic. Provenance: plan sections 7.2, 17.2, 22.1; AGENTS.md section 8.1.
close_reason: Implemented at c9fb756: root workspace + fr-core first slice (8 typed ID/generation types with compile-fail non-interchangeability proofs; ProtocolLimits with all section 17.2 ceilings, downward-only overrides, negotiation, checked arithmetic). Gates run remotely via rch at this revision: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 14 unit + 2 doc-tests pass. Independent review by AzureBasin caught and I fixed the per-viewer-budget floor bug (regression test included); self re-verification pass performed — peers may reopen on any failure.

title: xtask: verification lanes and the one fixed line-counting command
description:
WHY: The plan requires repository-owned build/test commands as the authority (GitHub-hosted Actions is never the correctness contract) and ONE fixed counting command so the 194k-line budget is tracked identically at every milestone and never redefined near the end.

SCOPE: xtask (or extension of scripts/verify.sh) providing: fmt/check/clippy/test lanes per crate and workspace; the counting command reporting handwritten Rust, generated bindings, non-Rust glue (JS/Swift/Kotlin, 20k allowance), vendored source, and project-induced upstream changes as SEPARATE numbers; wiring so the dispatch-only workflow manifest and dsr/act call these commands verbatim.

CONSTRAINTS: no unique correctness logic in YAML; lanes that cannot run yet refuse honestly (exit nonzero with a dormant message) rather than reporting a pass.

ACCEPTANCE: counting output is stable and documented; verify lanes green on the current tree; a planted over-budget fixture demonstrates the count actually measures what it claims. Provenance: plan sections 20.3, 22.2; AGENTS.md section 10.

ADDED SCOPE (polish round 1): a feature-resolved per-target dependency and unsafe audit lane (AGENTS sections 3.2/3.5, plan 19.1/20.1): for each build target (host desktop OSes, wasm32, mobile), resolve the actual feature graph and assert the target-specific rules — the browser build inherits no desktop FFI, the daemon inherits no GUI dependency, unsafe appears only in the named boundary crates, and direct/transitive/native/build-only/test-only dependencies are reported separately. A planted violation fixture (a test-only crate wrongly reachable from a shipping target) proves the lane catches drift.
close_reason: Implemented verification lanes (fast, docs, count, audit, crate, test-fixtures, release), fixed line counter (count.py) enforcing 194k target / 240k planned max / 250k hard stop and 20k glue allowance, feature-resolved target dependency & unsafe audit (audit.py), and planted negative fixture tests (test_verify_lanes.py). All checks and UBS pass cleanly.
